description: How computers process human language: tokenisation and text normalisation, n-gram and neural language models, word and sentence embeddings, text classification, sequence labelling, transformers and machine translation, with sustained attention to low-resource African languages such as Twi, Ewe and Hausa. Every model is built and probed in browser notebooks on real corpora, taught to the depth of a strong final-year NLP course.
modelledOn: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing
Eisenstein, Introduction to Natural Language Processing
Tunstall, von Werra and Wolf, Natural Language Processing with Transformers
Goldberg, Neural Network Methods for Natural Language Processing
outcomes: Build text-processing pipelines that tokenise, normalise and segment text in English and African languages, including subword tokenisers trained from scratch.
Implement and evaluate n-gram and neural language models and explain perplexity, smoothing and decoding strategies.
Train and compare word and sentence embeddings and use them for similarity search, classification and analysis of bias.
Design, train and evaluate text classifiers and sequence labellers with appropriate metrics and error analysis.
Explain the transformer architecture and fine-tune pretrained models for classification, tagging and machine translation.
Plan an NLP project for a low-resource language, covering data collection, annotation, evaluation and the ethics of language technology.

units.title: Text processing and tokenisation
topics: What makes language hard for computers: ambiguity, variation, Zipf's law, code-switching between English and Twi or Pidgin
Unicode, encodings and normalisation; diacritics and tone marks in Ewe and Yoruba; regular expressions for text cleaning
Word, sentence and morphological segmentation; stemming and lemmatisation; edit distance and spelling correction
Subword tokenisation: byte-pair encoding, WordPiece and unigram models trained and compared on an Akan corpus
Corpora and annotation: building a corpus from radio transcripts, news and social media; licensing and consent

units.title: Language models
topics: n-gram language models: the chain rule, Markov assumption, maximum likelihood estimates
Smoothing and backoff: Laplace, Kneser-Ney, interpolation; handling unknown words
Evaluation: perplexity, cross-entropy and their relation; intrinsic versus extrinsic evaluation
Neural language models: feedforward and recurrent models, LSTMs and GRUs, teacher forcing
Decoding: greedy, beam search, temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling; generating text and its failure modes

units.title: Word and sentence embeddings
topics: Distributional semantics: co-occurrence matrices, PMI, SVD-based word vectors
word2vec skip-gram and CBOW with negative sampling derived and implemented; GloVe and fastText subword vectors
Evaluating embeddings: similarity benchmarks, analogies, visualisation with t-SNE and UMAP
Contextual embeddings and sentence encoders: mean pooling, siamese networks, contrastive training
Semantic search and retrieval with vector indexes; bias measured in embedding spaces

units.title: Text classification
topics: Bag of words and TF-IDF features; naive Bayes and logistic regression baselines
Neural classifiers over embeddings; convolutional text classifiers; class imbalance
Sentiment analysis of Ghanaian tweets and mobile money customer complaints; topic and intent classification
Evaluation: precision, recall, macro and micro F1, confusion matrices, inter-annotator agreement with Cohen's kappa
Error analysis and robustness: adversarial inputs, spurious cues, out-of-domain text

units.title: Sequence labelling
topics: Part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition; BIO tagging schemes
Hidden Markov models and the Viterbi algorithm; forward-backward
Conditional random fields; BiLSTM-CRF taggers
Span-level evaluation; NER for Hausa, Yoruba and Swahili news text using community datasets
Dependency parsing in brief: transition-based parsing and Universal Dependencies treebanks

units.title: Attention and transformers
topics: Encoder-decoder models and attention; the alignment problem
The transformer: scaled dot-product and multi-head attention, positional encodings, layer normalisation, residual connections
Pretraining objectives: masked language modelling, causal language modelling, span corruption
Encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder families; multilingual models and their coverage of African languages
Fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation with adapters and LoRA, and prompting

units.title: Machine translation
topics: From rule-based and statistical translation to neural machine translation
Training a transformer translation model; data cleaning and parallel corpus alignment
Evaluation: BLEU, chrF and COMET; human evaluation of adequacy and fluency
Low-resource translation: back-translation, transfer from related languages, multilingual models; English to Twi and Ewe experiments
Speech in brief: automatic speech recognition and text-to-speech for languages with little written text

units.title: Working with African languages
topics: The landscape: over two thousand African languages; tone, noun classes, rich morphology and orthographic variation
Data scarcity: community data collection, crowdsourcing, participatory research and fair pay for annotators
Building resources: lexicons, morphological analysers, keyboards and spell checkers for Ghanaian languages
Benchmarking multilingual models on African languages and reporting results per language
Language technology for inclusion: health information, agricultural advisories and government services in local languages

units.title: Large language models, evaluation and ethics
topics: Scaling, instruction tuning and alignment in brief; retrieval-augmented generation
Evaluating generated text: hallucination, factuality, toxicity and benchmark contamination
Bias, representation and harms across languages and dialects; privacy of text data under the Data Protection Act
Capstone: an NLP system for a Ghanaian language with a datasheet, evaluation report and model card

schedule.title: Why language is hard: text basics
schedule.exercise: Short essay: three examples of ambiguity or code-switching in Ghanaian speech and what each does to a naive text-processing pipeline.

tasks.title: Count word frequencies in a text sample and plot rank against frequency on a log-log scale to check Zipf's law
Normalise a text with Ewe diacritics and tone marks to Unicode NFC, then write regular expressions that strip URLs and emojis
Implement Levenshtein edit distance and use it to build a spell corrector with a dictionary, evaluating it on 50 misspelled words

schedule.title: Subword tokenisation and corpora
schedule.exercise: Write a short corpus plan: sources, licensing, consent and annotation guidelines for a Twi corpus built from radio transcripts.

tasks.title: Train a byte-pair encoding tokeniser on a small Akan text for 200 merges and print the first 20 merges it learns
Compare BPE and unigram tokenisers on an Akan corpus by vocabulary size and tokens per word, and explain what each does to rare words
Build a cleaned, deduplicated corpus from raw news and radio transcript samples and report its size, language mix and consent status

schedule.title: n-gram language models
schedule.exercise: Compute bigram probabilities and perplexity for a small corpus by hand, then check with code.

tasks.title: Estimate bigram probabilities from a 1,000-word corpus and use them to score two candidate sentences
Add Laplace smoothing and Kneser-Ney style interpolation to a trigram model and compare held-out perplexity of each approach
Evaluate unigram, bigram and trigram models by perplexity on held-out text and explain why the lowest perplexity may not help a downstream task

schedule.title: Neural language models and decoding
schedule.exercise: Short analysis: compare text generated with greedy, beam and nucleus sampling and describe the failure modes you observe.

tasks.title: Train a small recurrent language model on a character corpus with teacher forcing and plot its training and validation loss
Implement greedy, beam search and top-p decoding and show how temperature changes the diversity of the generated text
Compare an LSTM and a GRU language model on the same corpus for equal parameter budgets and report perplexity and generation quality

schedule.title: Word embeddings
schedule.exercise: Compute a PMI matrix for a small corpus, factorise it and interpret the nearest words for five terms.

tasks.title: Build a co-occurrence matrix from a small corpus, convert to PPMI and list the nearest neighbours of three words by cosine similarity
Implement skip-gram with negative sampling in NumPy, train for 20 epochs and check that related words move closer together
Evaluate embeddings with similarity benchmarks and analogies, visualise them with t-SNE and compare word2vec with fastText on rare words

schedule.title: Sentence embeddings and retrieval
schedule.exercise: Design a semantic search for a clinic's FAQ in Twi and English and list the failure cases you expect.

tasks.title: Build sentence vectors by mean-pooling word embeddings and rank ten sentences by similarity to a query
Index 500 short documents in a vector index and evaluate retrieval by recall at 5 against a keyword search baseline
Measure gender or profession bias in an embedding space with a similarity test and try one debiasing step, reporting its effect on task quality

schedule.title: Text classification
schedule.exercise: Annotate 50 mobile money complaints, compute inter-annotator agreement and write down the guideline changes that raise it.

tasks.title: Build a TF-IDF plus naive Bayes baseline for sentiment on 300 labelled tweets and report accuracy and the confusion matrix
Classify mobile money customer complaints into intents with logistic regression and a neural model, and compare macro F1 under class imbalance
Find five spurious cues and adversarial edits that fool a sentiment classifier, retrain with fixes and test on out-of-domain text

schedule.title: Sequence labelling
schedule.exercise: Run the Viterbi algorithm by hand on a three-word sentence with a small HMM, then evaluate span-level NER on news text.

tasks.title: Convert a short NER annotation into BIO tags and decode a tag sequence back into entity spans
Implement the Viterbi algorithm for a part-of-speech HMM and measure tagging accuracy on a small treebank
Train an NER tagger on Hausa or Yoruba news text from a community dataset and report span-level precision, recall and F1 per entity type

schedule.title: Attention and the transformer
schedule.exercise: Hand-calculate attention weights for a three-token input and annotate a transformer block diagram with tensor shapes.

tasks.title: Implement dot-product attention over an encoder's states and print the attention weights for a four-word source sentence
Implement multi-head self-attention with positional encodings and a causal mask in NumPy and unit-test its output shapes and masking
Pretrain a tiny transformer with a masked language modelling objective and a causal objective on the same corpus and compare their strengths

schedule.title: Pretrained models and adaptation
schedule.exercise: Short report: which pretrained models cover your target African language, and how would you adapt one with limited data and compute?

tasks.title: Tokenise sentences in Twi, Ewe, Hausa and English with a multilingual tokeniser and compare token counts per word
Fine-tune a small pretrained encoder on a labelled classification task using a LoRA-style adapter and compare it with full fine-tuning
Benchmark a multilingual model on classification in three African languages and explain gaps in coverage by tokeniser fertility and pretraining data

schedule.title: Machine translation
schedule.exercise: Short comparison: rule-based, statistical and neural translation for English to Twi, with an example of where each fails.

tasks.title: Build a word-for-word dictionary translator for ten English sentences into Twi and list the errors from word order and idioms
Compute BLEU and chrF for ten translations against references and explain why chrF is fairer for morphologically rich languages
Train a small English to Twi translation model with back-translation of monolingual text and measure the BLEU gain over the baseline

schedule.title: African language technology
schedule.exercise: Write a participatory research plan for collecting speech or text data in a Ghanaian community with fair pay and informed consent.

tasks.title: Analyse a Twi or Yoruba text for tone marks, noun classes or affixes with regular expressions and summarise morphological variation
Build a simple spell checker and a keyboard layout map for a Ghanaian language from a word list and evaluate its recall
Benchmark a model on classification and NER in five African languages and report results per language with confidence intervals

schedule.title: Large language models and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: a datasheet, evaluation report and model card for an NLP system in a Ghanaian language.

tasks.title: Build a small retrieval-augmented question answering system over ten short health documents and show the retrieved passages beside each answer
Evaluate a generative system for hallucination and toxicity with a hand-labelled test set and check whether the test set leaked into training
Complete an NLP system for a Ghanaian language with data collection plan, evaluation per dialect, datasheet and model card, and report limitations
